pamphlet_excerpts: Adding Small Photographs: Adding small photographs to your pedigree chart can make it moreinteresting.
Buy Charts Spaces: You can buy charts with spaces built in for photos, or youcan design your own.
Photo Ancestor Near: Place a photo of each ancestor near his or herspace on the chart; do not worry if you don’t have a photo of each one.
Pedigree Chart Contains: Your pedigree chart contains information about your parents, grandparents, and other direct ancestors.
step_by_step_procedure: But Other relatives Brothers: But what about other relatives such as brothers, sisters, uncles, aunts, and cousins?.
They Too Part: They, too, are an important part of your genealogy.
Form Record Information: The form used to record information about them is called a family group record form.
Slightly Different Formats: Slightly different formats are available, but they all show thesame basic information.

pamphlet_excerpts: Easiest Placeto Start: The easiest placeto start your family history is with your own history.
Canbegin Life Story: You canbegin your life story by doing some of the following activities.
Write Journal Regular: You should write in your journal on a regular basis, everyday, every week, or every month.
Log Activities Thoughts: It is a log of your activities, thoughts, and feelings.
step_by_step_procedure: Personal History Life: A personal history, or life story, tells about what happened inthe past.
Include Quotes Stories: It may include quotes or stories from your journal ordiary.
Small Way Writing: In a small way, writing about your own and your family’shistory helps preserve the history of our nation.
Anne Frank: A Diary of Hope Amid Tragedy One of the finest examples of a young personrecording their life story is Anne Frank.

pamphlet_excerpts: Then Tofind Accurate: Then you must know where to go tofind accurate answers.
Family Movedto United: If your family movedto the United States from another country, it is important to askyour parents or guardians and other relatives.
Not Formally Interviewing: Even if you are not formally interviewing allthese people, write down or record the information they tell you.
Not Information Someone: Not all the information someone tells you is necessarilycorrect.
step_by_step_procedure: Relationships Great-uncle: Relationships (such as great-uncle Ralph was Grandpa Erickson’s brother) are usually correct.
But Names Places: But names, places, and dates may not be accurate.
Double-check Information: Double-check the information you gather against other records.
Fun Talk Themand: It can be fun to talk to themand discover what they have and to hear what they know.

Ancestral Family: Ancestral family organizations are created around anancestral couple and include all of their descendants.
Forexample John Jane: Forexample, John and Jane Clough who came to America in theearly 1600s are the center of a Clough family organization.
step_by_step_procedure: Everyone Belongs: Everyone who belongs to this organization should be ableto trace his or her ancestry to this couple.
Purposes Afamily: The purposes of afamily organization are to do good research into the ancestryand descendants of a couple and to record and share theinformation.
Organization Publishes: Such an organization often publishes extensivefamily genealogies and newsletters that may be available insome major libraries.
Surname Organization Based: A surname organization is based on a surname that isassociated with a specific geographical area and time period.

Typed Grave Rose: If you just typed in grave and Rose Goldman, you would get thousands of hits.
Youmight Add Name: To do this, youmight add the name of the place Rose Goldman died or the year of herdeath to your search terms.
Remember However Not: Remember, however, that not all the Rose Goldmans you find will be your ancestor.
step_by_step_procedure: Fact Possible Noneof: In fact, it is possible that noneof the matches you get will be your ancestor.
Remember Too Computers: Remember, too, that computers are not as smart as you are.
Forinstance Suppose Looking: Forinstance, suppose you are looking for your ancestor named Marco Angelo Benedetto.
Type His Name: You type his name into the search engine, and it doesnot find him.

step_by_step_procedure: But Other relatives Brothers: But what about other relatives such as brothers, sisters, uncles, aunts, and cousins?.
They Too Part: They, too, are an important part of your genealogy.
Form Record Information: The form used to record information about them is called a family group record form.

pamphlet_excerpts: Todaythe FHL Largest: Todaythe FHL is the largest genealogical library in theworld and is open to the general public.
Anyonecan Library Resources: Anyonecan use the library’s resources free of charge.
Inaddition Thousands: Inaddition, thousands of associated branch librariescalled Family History Centers are located through outthe world.
Family History Centers: Family History Centers are often locatedin local meetinghouses of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and staffed by volunteers.
step_by_step_procedure: History Centers Computers: Most Family History Centers have computers within ternet access to genealogy websites.
FHL Collection Includes: The FHL’s collection includes more than twomillion rolls of microfilm and thousands of boundbooks.
New Microfilm Genealogical: New microfilm of genealogical records fromall over the world is continually being made.
Library Holdings Described: All of the library’s holdings are described inthe FamilySearch Catalog, which is available on theinternet at familysearch.org.

pamphlet_excerpts: Then Tofind Accurate: Then you must know where to go tofind accurate answers.
Family Movedto United: If your family movedto the United States from another country, it is important to askyour parents or guardians and other relatives.
Not Formally Interviewing: Even if you are not formally interviewing allthese people, write down or record the information they tell you.
Not Information Someone: Not all the information someone tells you is necessarilycorrect.
step_by_step_procedure: Relationships Great-uncle: Relationships (such as great-uncle Ralph was Grandpa Erickson’s brother) are usually correct.
But Names Places: But names, places, and dates may not be accurate.
Double-check Information: Double-check the information you gather against other records.
Fun Talk Themand: It can be fun to talk to themand discover what they have and to hear what they know.
